newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: British critic due in Switzerland over Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: British critic due in Switzerland over Nazi gold.

text.p: A leading British critic of Swiss gold purchases from Nazi Germany is to visit Switzerland later this month and meet parliament's foreign policy commissions, officials said on Wednesday.

A parliament statement said foreign policy experts from both chambers would meet Greville Janner, an opposition Labour member of the British parliament and vice-president of the World Jewish Congress, when he visits "in the course of November".
There were no more details on the talks or who else Janner would meet. Officials said the dates for the trip had not yet been fixed.

In London, the Holocaust Education Trust which Janner chairs said he would be in Switzerland to press for renegotiation of a 1946 agreement between Berne and the Allied powers on dividing looted Nazi gold.
Berne has rejected the possibility of renegotiating a valid international treaty 50 years later.

Janner pressured the British government into releasing a report in September that revived memories of the 1946 pact, which forced Switzerland to pay the Allies a portion of the Nazi gold bought by the Swiss National Bank during World War Two.

The Swiss National Bank acknowledged in 1985 that it had bought gold worth 1.2 billion Swiss francs at 1940s prices from the Nazi German Reichsbank despite suspicions that some of it had been stolen from countries occupied by Hitler's troops.
